The Magnificent Seven is a group of tech (or tech-adjacent) companies that are among the leaders in their respective industries and have delivered outstanding long-term returns. It includes Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA).

Their performances have been fairly mixed and volatile this year. Tesla is in the red, while Microsoft and Meta also spent significant time in negative year-to-date return territory before recently bouncing back.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

It's always worth keeping an eye on these stocks, but there are plenty of lesser-known companies that have performed much better than the Magnificent Seven and, according to average Wall Street price targets, still have significant room to run. Let's consider two such examples: Revolution Medicines (NASDAQ:RVMD) and Oruka Therapeutics (NASDAQ:ORKA). Both have more than doubled this year, but are they worth investing in at current levels? Let's find out.

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Revolution Medicines

Revolution Medicines, an oncology-focused biotech, made a significant breakthrough this year. The company earned approval for Rasonque, a medicine for certain patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer.

Rasonque targets RAS-driven cancers (RAS is a protein), which were long considered very challenging to treat effectively. But Revolution Medicines has cracked the code.

In a Phase 3 study comparing it with the current standard of care, cytotoxic chemotherapy, Rasonque led to a median overall survival of 13.2 months versus 6.7 months for cytotoxic chemotherapy in patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer. The recent approval in this indication may only be the beginning.

Revolution Medicines is testing Rasonque across several other potential indications, including lung cancer. According to some analysts, Rasonque could generate $15.1 billion in sales for pancreatic cancer alone by 2034. And if it earns indications across other fields, it may rack up $20.8 billion in total peak revenue.

With projections like those, it's no wonder Revolution Medicines' shares have soared this year, and the company is also developing other candidates. Revolution Medicines is clearly a promising stock, but is it too expensive at current levels?

title: Tesla readies flying Roadster reveal in Texas to re-energize car business

Tesla readies flying Roadster reveal in Texas to re-energize car business
Luke Juricic
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:25 AM PDT 2 min read
TSLA
SPCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Tesla Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA) is preparing to unveil its long-delayed Roadster sports car in Texas on Thursday, turning to a high-stakes flight demonstration in a bid to re-energize its core automobile business. The event, scheduled to take place at a SpaceX rocket testing facility near Waco, aims to showcase a prototype equipped with technology designed to briefly lift the vehicle off the ground.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The dramatic presentation arrives at a critical juncture for the electric vehicle manufacturer following two consecutive years of annual sales declines. While Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk has increasingly focused on long-term artificial intelligence and autonomous robotics initiatives, automotive sales continue to generate the vast majority of the company's total revenue and operating profits.

A commercially available flying vehicle remains highly improbable due to severe regulatory hurdles, safety concerns, and prohibitive manufacturing costs. Instead, the spectacle serves primarily as a high-visibility marketing catalyst intended to reinforce Tesla's reputation as an industry innovator while drawing attention back to its consumer lineup.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The new Roadster re-enters a narrow vehicle portfolio that currently relies almost entirely on the mass-market Model 3 sedan and Model Y crossover. With older models recently phased out and the Cybertruck contributing modest volumes, the addition expands options alongside niche offerings like the commercial Semi and the unreleased Cybercab.

First announced in 2017, the second-generation Roadster has suffered years of production delays and shifting timelines. By reviving the nameplate that marked Tesla's entry into the automotive industry in 2008, management is attempting to recapture the brand momentum that originally defined its market trajectory.

Whether the demonstration translates into sustained consumer demand remains the central question for market watchers. Investors will be closely watching whether Thursday's event can reignite broader interest in Tesla's automotive segment or if it simply underscores the growing reliance on promotional stunts amid broader operational headwinds.
